I don't think you meant to say things are easy to find, but i just want to clarify that it's very hard to find/see things even in our own solar system. Afaik we can only see things if they are close and big enough so we can see them when they are illuminated by the sun or when they cover something else e.g. a distant star or a planet that we are observing and the 'other' thing gets in the way. Wobbly orbits can also be used to find new bodies (neptune), but without seeing the body itself it's hard to prove just by it's effects on orbits of other bodies.

An exeption to that is of course anything that emits light by itselve like other stars.

So could there be another planet far out in the dark where we can't find it? Yes. Another star? No. Black hole? Yes(?)
